text:
alex: Heads-up — multiple Dedicated clusters reporting p99 token latency spike starting ~00:12 UTC. Alerts from customer-facing routes + internal SLO dashboards. Noticing heavy tail on GPUs in eu-west-1.
maya: saw it too on the dashboard. p95 up 2.4x, p99 ~3.1x for small-gen workloads. Any recent infra changes?
deploy-bot: rolling-update completed: gpu-runtime:release/2024.11.07 -> 2024.11.08 @ 00:05 UTC
alex: that rolled out to dedicated pools in eu-west-1 at 00:05. It included driver update nvcc-driver-525.23 and firmware fw_gk210_2.1.0.
jordan: pinging infra — what exact driver/firmware? Could be NVMe/host IO interaction after driver page cache changes.
linda: opened a support escalation with a customer who noticed increased API latency around the same time. They've provided traces showing lots of queueing on token generation.
kevin: repro steps from the customer: steady stream of 1k short requests (avg 60 tokens), p99 diverges after ~20 minutes. They also saw host IO bursts coincident with the spike.
maya: putting up quick triage checklist:
- confirm rollout targets and start times (alex: done)
- check GPU firmware+driver changelog
- check host kernel messages (dmesg) for NVMe/IO errors
- capture perf traces / nvtop / iostat from affected hosts
jordan: grabbing host metrics now. iostat shows NVMe avg await jumping from 1ms -> 12ms at 00:12 UTC on node gpu-wek-07.
alex: nvmetool logs show a burst of write latency + io queue depth rising. Could be backup job or snapshot coinciding.
maya: checking k8s daemonsets — snapshot job from backup-service started at 00:10 UTC in eu-west-1 — incremental backups to local NVMe.
kevin: that backup job wasn't expected on Dedicated pools. Looks like a mis-scoped cron from infra images.
linda: customer suggested repro by running a synthetic load while triggering a local disk-heavy job — we should try to reproduce in staging.
jordan: short mitigation idea: throttle backup-service on nodes that are flagged as serving inference. Workaround: add taint to Dedicated GPUs nodes so cron doesn't schedule.
alex: immediate mitigations proposed:
- rollback GPU driver to 524.x on the smallest subset (canary) — lower risk than full rollback
- throttle backup cron (disable for dedicated node pool)
- increase eviction/queue buffer on serving runtime for short term
- enable fallback routing to warm dedicated hosts in other region (eu-central)
maya: I can push a policy to pause backup cron across dedicated node selectors. Doing that now.
deploy-bot: job "backup-service-cron" paused for nodeSelector:dedicated=true @ 00:30 UTC
jordan: after pause, NVMe await dropped back to ~1.8ms on gpu-wek-07 within 90s. p99 on affected route fell from 3.1x back to ~1.1x within 5 mins.
alex: good rollback test — but we still need to validate driver/firmware interaction. Can we reproduce with synthetic load + explicit fio pattern?
kevin: setting up staging run: 2000 qps short requests + fio random write 4k 70% rw on the same host. Will report in 15.
linda: also gathering dmesg and firmware logs. If firmware had a changed IO scheduler default that could cause compaction pauses.
jordan: FYI: kernel 6.4 kernel upgrade on some hosts earlier this week changed bio concurrency heuristics. Might be 3-way interaction: kernel + driver + background IO.
maya: ok capture plan:
1) fio + synthetic load in staging (kevin)
2) perf + nvtop logs + iostat (jordan)
3) collect kernel oops/dmesg + nvme smart logs (linda)
4) if repro, test driver rollback vs pinning to older kernel via boot image (alex)
kevin: staging run started. Initial 5-min baseline looks fine. Now starting fio at 00:47.
kevin: after 3 minutes, we see nvme await climb and token latency tail rising. Repro successful in staging.
alex: that confirms host IO spikes cause the p99 tail for small requests. Need durable fixes:
- prevent noisy IO on inference hosts (taint + scheduling rules)
- ensure backup-service uses remote block storage not local NVMe for dedicated pools
- add runtime-level isolation: limit host IO per pod via cgroup io.weight
jordan: added an emergency cgroup rule to throttle backup-service on staging, reduced IO impact significantly.
maya: follow-ups assigned:
- infra (alex/jordan): roll driver rollback plan for a narrow canary and validate (ETA 3h)
- infra (linda): audit cron jobs and image config for nodeSelector leakage (ETA 2h)
- platform (maya): add pod-level IO throttling defaults and node taints for dedicated pools (ETA 24h)
- support (linda): update customer with status and temporary routing/fallback we applied (ETA 30m)
alex: I'll draft rollback playbook. If rollback not possible quickly, we'll keep backup-service paused and escalate to product for longer-term config change.
linda: customer update sent: "We're investigating a transient p99 regression tied to host-level disk activity. We've paused the background job affecting your pool and are validating remediation. ETA ~1 hour." :thumbsup:
sre-oncall: marking incident P2 for now. If we see reoccurrence after re-enabling backups, escalate to P1.
alex: closing loop — good catch on the cron. We'll document the three-way interaction in postmortem (kernel+driver+local IO) and follow the mitigation list.
maya: tracking ticket created INF-4729 to prevent local NVMe backups on inference-dedicated pools.
kevin: thanks team — staging repro and pause look good. Will loop back after driver canary or further changes.
